# DKR-011: Socket proxies do not allow writes

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

A socket proxy is only a boundary if it refuses writes. With POST enabled, a client can create and start containers, which is root on the host; EXEC runs commands in any container. stackward reads only the permission flag names and boolean values from a socket proxy's environment, nothing else.

## Verify by hand

```sh
docker inspect --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' <socket-proxy> | grep -E '^(POST|EXEC)='
```

## How to fix it

Set POST=0 and EXEC=0, and enable only the read sections the client needs (for example CONTAINERS=1, NETWORKS=1). If a client truly needs writes, give it its own proxy with the narrowest flags and keep it off shared networks.

## What a fix can break

Clients that start, stop or update containers through the proxy (auto updaters, PaaS agents) stop doing so.
